Why Are There Tigers in Siberia? The Ice Age Journey of the Amur Tiger #map #maps #geography #funfacts #tiger #tigers #animals  Ever wondered why tigers roam the icy forests of Siberia? It all started 2 million years ago in northern China. As tigers spread across Asia, they adapted to jungles, grasslands—and eventually, the frozen north. During the Ice Age, herds of prey moved into Siberia, and tigers followed. They evolved thicker fur, larger bodies, and became the Amur tiger—built to survive the cold. Some even pushed west into the Caucasus and Iran, becoming the now-extinct Caspian tiger. From tropical hunters to snow-covered predators, this is the wild journey of how tigers conquered Siberia.

Sa couleur est due à une anomalie génétique appelée leucisme, obtenue par consanguinité 😳🚨 Dans la nature, un tigre blanc aurait peu de chances de survie : il ne peut pas se camoufler et souffre souvent de problèmes physiques et comportementaux 🌿 🗓️ Dès 2028, en France, il sera interdit de détenir des animaux sauvages dans les cirques. Cette interdiction est due à la loi contre la maltraitance animale de novembre 2021. It's thought that each vocalisation is used to communicate different things. 2. They are protective over their kill.  Tigers don't usually eat their prey at the kill site - but instead drag their prey into cover to feed. If a tiger leaves - say to get a drink - it will cover it's kill by raking leaves, dirt, grass and even rocks over the carcass. 3. Tigers primarily hunt deer, but as opportunistic predators, they can also eat wild boars, birds, fish, rodents, amphibians, reptiles, and even insects.
